headline: Baipu breaks ground with TSMC expected in two buildings by late 2029
deck: Kaohsiung marked the park on 21 September. Reuters attaches two TSMC buildings and a Q4 2029 start that the city note does not repeat.
body: Kaohsiung formally broke ground on the Baipu industrial park on 21 September. The city government puts the site at about 88.73 hectares in total, with about 53 hectares planned for industrial use [E2]. Reuters, covering the same ceremony, gives 88.7 hectares overall and 53.6 hectares of industrial land, and says TSMC is expected to occupy the park with two buildings whose facilities are expected to begin operations in the fourth quarter of 2029 [E1].

The municipal note that records the groundbreaking does not itself state the two-building occupancy or the Q4 2029 operating target; those details are in the Reuters account of the same park [E1][E2]. Reuters says TSMC is expected to occupy two buildings while the city government will build factory facilities [E1].

Reuters frames the park around advanced packaging capacity anchored by TSMC. The city describes an industrial park whose majority of land is reserved for industrial use, without restating the foundry's occupancy calendar [E1][E2].

What stands on the day's notes is the ceremony and the occupancy dates already attached to it: groundbreaking on 21 September, and Reuters' expected start of operations in the fourth quarter of 2029 for the two TSMC buildings [E1][E2].
